v.why: Adding a conv on the direct input-to-output edge helps far more when that edge was empty (often reconnecting a disconnected cell) than when it replaces an existing op (exps 6-10 vs 1-5).
Replacing the direct skip with a conv removes a useful residual path and was consistently negative across datasets (exps 1-5).
Removing edge 3 when edge 4 is absent leaves fewer routes to the output and can disconnect the cell, causing much larger drops (exps 21, 22, 29).
With edge 5 absent, edge 3 is a primary path to the output, so deleting it is far more damaging (exps 21, 23, 29).
Adding a skip on an empty direct edge restores connectivity and gradient flow, whereas replacing a conv with skip loses capacity (exps 81, 85 vs 86, 87, 90).
Turning an empty edge 5 into skip opens a route from node 2 to the output, while replacing a conv on edge 5 with skip discards capacity (exps 45, 50 vs 46, 47, 49).
Downgrading the edge-5 3x3 conv to an identity consistently hurt accuracy, especially on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet16 (exps 43, 47, 49).
Swapping a parameter-free pooling op on the last edge for a 3x3 conv adds substantial capacity and gave large gains (exps 11-18).
Replacing a 3x3 conv on the node1-to-node2 edge with pooling removes learned features, unlike replacing none, skip, or 1x1 (exp 58 vs 55-57).
When the direct input-to-output edge is missing, adding a conv on node1-to-output adds a critical output path, giving larger gains (exps 91, 92 vs 93-100).

- **When an edit matters most.** Edits matter most when they connect or disconnect the only route from input to output. The +75-point jumps in experiments 6, 85 and 91, and the -78 drop in experiment 21, all happen at that boundary.
- **Replacing a conv usually hurts.** Swapping a nor_conv_3x3 on a key edge for skip_connect or avg_pool_3x3 tends to lower accuracy. Replacing none or avg_pool with a conv tends to raise it.

The hypotheses are not independently verified. Some conditions are only backed by 1–2 experiments, so treat them as likely, not confirmed.
